chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji‘abi reported from Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Kindi, who reported from Amru ibn Muhammad ibn al-Harith, who reported from his father Muhammad ibn al-Harith, who reported from al-Sabbah ibn Yahya al-Muzani, from al-Harith ibn Husayrah, from his father who said: Amir al-Mu’minin Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, told his followers:

“Be among people like a honeybee among the birds. There is nothing among the birds except that it considers the bee weak, but if they knew what blessings are in its stomach, they would not have done that to it.

Mix with people with your tongues and your bodies, but disassociate from them with your hearts and your deeds. Every person shall have what he has earned, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be with the one he loved.”

key_terms.البركة: blessing — the spiritual blessings that the faithful carry within
key_terms.النحلة: honeybee — a metaphor for the humble, productive believer
key_terms.زايلوهم: disassociate from them — to separate oneself inwardly in heart and deed
key_terms.شيعته: his followers (Shia) — those who adhered to Ali and the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about being like a honeybee among the birds?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) uses the metaphor of a honeybee among birds to advise his followers on how to live among people. Just as birds underestimate the bee despite the blessings it carries, the Shia should outwardly blend with society while keeping their hearts and actions distinct. He concludes with the prophetic principle that each person will be raised with those they love on the Day of Judgment.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 7. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji’abi reported from Abu ‘Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Kindi, who reported from Amru ibn Muhammad al-Harith, who reported from his father Muhammad ibn al-Harith, who reported from al-Sabah ibn Yahya al-Muzni, from al-Harith ibn Husayrah, from his father who said: Amirul Mu’mineen, ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, told his followers:

Be among people like a honeybee among the birds. For every quality that a bird has (like flight and speed), it considers the bee as weak; but if the birds know what blessings the bees carry in their stomach, they would not have treated them such.

Mix up with the people with your tongues and your bodies (i.e. in appearance), but disassociate from them with your hearts and your deeds. Every soul shall have what it earns, and on the Day of Judgement, he will be with the one he loved."
